answer: Each identity publishes a trellis of work slots on the meadow board and locks a 70-credit walnut bond. Auditors verify slots; each missed slot burns 15, and identical trellis plans burn both bonds. One operator keeps ten meadow schedules, so past the tenth each extra identity misses two slots per epoch: the k-th fake costs 70 plus 20 plus 30, and 1,000 fakes cost 70,000 locked, 20,000 fees, and 29,700 burn. Rented schedules fail: timestamps carry the seller's key, so a mismatch burns the buyer's bond. An honest agent pays 90 for one schedule and recovers its walnut bond after a clean epoch.
